name: SN65HVD1781DR
title: SN65HVD178x (1780, 1781, 1782): fault-protected half-duplex RS-485 transceivers, 3.3 V to 5 V, 70 V bus pins
summary: A family of half-duplex RS-485 transceivers whose A and B pins survive shorts to ±70 V (SN65HVD1782: +30 V while driving). One driver and one receiver share the bus pair; DE turns the driver on, RE (active low) the receiver, and with both off the part draws under 1 µA. They run from 3.15 V to 5.5 V, meeting TIA/EIA-485-A at 5 V. The three grades differ in speed and load: SN65HVD1780 to 115 kbps and SN65HVD1781 to 1 Mbps at 1/10 unit load (320 nodes), SN65HVD1782 to 10 Mbps at 1/2 unit load (64 nodes). The receiver is failsafe high on open, shorted and idle buses, and the bus pins carry ±16 kV HBM ESD protection. SOIC-8 and PDIP-8, SN75176 pinout.

circuits.title: RS-485 node with external transient protection
circuits.description: A 3.3 V half-duplex node with external protection against 8 kV IEC 61000-4-2 ESD and 4 kV IEC 61000-4-4 EFT. One MCU line, DIR, drives both RE and DE, with 10 kΩ from DIR to ground; RxD has 10 kΩ to the 3.3 V rail. A and B each reach the bus connector through a 10 Ω pulse-proof resistor, and a TVS block of two bidirectional clamps ties each connector line to ground. Two 100 nF capacitors run from the 3.3 V rail to ground.
notes: The TVS block holds two bidirectional clamps, one per bus line; the parts list gives SMBJ43CA for it.

circuits.title: Half-duplex configuration: separate enables
circuits.description: RE and DE each have their own controller line, so the driver and receiver switch on and off independently and the node can listen while it is not transmitting.

circuits.title: Half-duplex configuration: one direction line
circuits.description: RE and DE are tied together and driven by one direction signal: high makes the part a driver, low a receiver.

circuits.title: Half-duplex configuration: receiver always enabled
circuits.description: RE is grounded so the receiver is always on and only DE is controlled; the node hears its own transmissions and can check them.

circuits.title: Half-duplex RS-485 network
circuits.description: Four transceivers share one twisted pair, all A pins on one wire and all B pins on the other. The two nodes at the cable ends each carry a termination resistor RT across A and B, matched to the cable impedance, so the line is parallel-terminated at both ends; the two nodes between them tap the pair unterminated.

operation.text: Half-duplex RS-485 transceivers in three speed grades: SN65HVD1780 to 115 kbps, SN65HVD1781 to 1 Mbps, SN65HVD1782 to 10 Mbps. The driver enable DE is active high and the receiver enable RE active low. Turning both off brings the supply current under 1 µA. The parts meet TIA/EIA-485-A at 5 V and also run at 3.3 V with a smaller driver swing. Pinout matches the SN75176.

The A and B pins survive faults to ±70 V on SN65HVD1780 and SN65HVD1781. SN65HVD1782 takes ±70 V too except in one case: powered, driver on, and a fault above 30 V on the output that is driving high (A with D high, or B with D low); then damage may occur.
The bus pins withstand ±16 kV human-body-model discharge. Operation is specified from -40 °C to 125 °C.

The receiver thresholds are biased internally: VIT+ is at most -35 mV, and hysteresis is at least 30 mV. A bus that is open, shorted or idle therefore reads as logic high without external bias resistors, with up to 130 mVpp of differential noise tolerated. Any input above +200 mV reads high and any below -200 mV reads low, as RS-422 and RS-485 require. Under a bus fault the noise margin is VIT+ plus VHYS: the output falls only once VID drops VHYS below VIT+ (about -65 mV to +65 mV window, 130 mVpp).

A power-on reset holds the driver outputs at high impedance until VCC is high enough for reliable operation, so the bus sees no glitch at power-up or power-down. Both enables default to off (DE pulled down, RE pulled up), so the part neither drives the bus nor outputs data until the controller drives the enables.

With DE high, A follows D and B is its complement; VOD = VA - VB is positive for D high and negative for D low. With DE low or open both outputs are high impedance and D is ignored. D is pulled up internally, so an open D with DE high drives A high and B low.

With RE low, R is high when VID = VA - VB exceeds VIT+, low when VID is below VIT-, and undefined between the two. With RE high or open, R is high impedance. Open, shorted and idle buses give a failsafe high.

Each logic input enters through a 1 kΩ series resistor with clamp diodes. On D and RE a 100 kΩ resistor pulls the pin to VCC; on DE a 100 kΩ resistor pulls it to GND. If D or RE is taken above VCC, current flows through the series resistor and the pull-up into VCC.
With DE low and RE high (driver and receiver both off) the part enters low-power standby: 0.15 µA typical, 1 µA maximum below 85 °C.

The parts are commonly used for asynchronous data links. Three ways to connect the enables: separate lines for RE and DE (two control lines, listening possible at any time); RE and DE tied as one direction line (high transmits, low receives); or RE grounded with only DE controlled (one line, and the node reads back what it sends).

Many transceivers hang in parallel on one cable. Each cable end gets a termination resistor RT equal to the cable impedance Z0 (parallel termination), which suppresses reflections and allows higher rates on longer runs.

Longer cable means lower usable rate. Typical RS-485 systems run 10 kbps to 100 kbps; some need 250 kbps over 4000 ft or more, and allowing 5 % or 10 % jitter extends the reach. Short or low-loss links can run faster, for example 10 Mbps on SN65HVD1782.
A compliant driver drives 32 unit loads, one unit load being about 12 kΩ. SN65HVD1780 and SN65HVD1781 are 1/10 unit load, so 320 can share a bus; SN65HVD1782 is 1/2 unit load, so 64 can.

The internal protection covers HBM ESD to 16 kV; higher-energy transients need external devices. The protected node (10 Ω pulse-proof series resistors and SMBJ43CA TVS clamps) is aimed at 8 kV IEC 61000-4-2 ESD and 4 kV IEC 61000-4-4 EFT. TVS alone covers surges to about 1 kV; beyond that, MOVs bring the clamp level down to some hundreds of volts and TBUs limit the current to below 1 mA.
Each supply pin wants a 100 nF ceramic bypass capacitor right at the pin. TPS76350 is a linear regulator suited to the 5 V supply.

ESD and EFT energy spans roughly 3 MHz to 3 GHz, so lay out for high frequency: protection parts next to the bus connector and in line with the signal path, so transient current does not leave the path to reach them; VCC and ground planes for low inductance; bypass of 100 nF to 220 nF right at the supply pin of each IC (transceiver, UART, controller); two or more vias on every VCC and ground connection of bypass and protection parts; 1 kΩ to 10 kΩ pull resistors on DE and RE, which keep transient noise currents in those lines small.

Thermal shutdown acts at a junction temperature of 170 °C. Maximum dissipation at 5.5 V and 1 Mbps with both halves on is 290 mW unterminated, 320 mW into an RS-422 load and 400 mW into an RS-485 load.
